name: MD-04
label: Safe D

key_factors: PVI of D+39 makes this one of the most Democratic districts in the country
Incumbent Glenn Ivey running with strong fundraising ($674K raised, $459K on hand)
Republican challenger George McDermott is underfunded and unknown
model.rationale: The baseline of D+32.4 rests on an overwhelming partisan lean, incumbency, and a large money advantage, with no contrary evidence in polls, ratings, or headlines. I keep the baseline essentially intact, shading p_dem to 0.99 to reflect residual uncertainty.
model.watch: A major scandal or unexpected incumbent retirement would be the only plausible path to making this competitive.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Maryland's 4th District is a heavily Democratic seat centered in Prince George's County, with a partisan lean of roughly D+39. Incumbent Glenn Ivey is running for reelection after winning the seat in 2022, and he holds a substantial financial edge, having raised about $674,000 with $459,000 on hand.

His Republican opponent, George McDermott, reports no fundraising, and there is no outside spending, polling, or expert rating activity suggesting the race is competitive. Prediction markets price a Democratic win at 97 percent. With no evidence cutting against the fundamentals-based forecast, this race remains safely Democratic, with the main uncertainty being turnout-driven variation in the final margin rather than the outcome itself.
